Ukraine, Russia Agree Ceasefire Timetable for Oleshky Mission — Ukrainian Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets has announced an agreement between Kyiv and Moscow to enact a synchronized localized ceasefire in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky starting Tuesday, Oct. 27, at 3:00 a.m. Kyiv time (4:00 a.m. Moscow time).

Ukraine Is Winning Time on the Battlefield, But Can It Win the Battle for Its Future? — Ukraine is demonstrating remarkable resilience on the battlefield while facing mounting economic, political, demographic and social pressures. Now it must secure its future.

Molodist Film Festival Marks 55 Years, Bringing International Cinema to Kyiv Oct. 24-Nov. 1 — Founded in 1970 as a two-day showcase of student short films, the Molodist International Film Festival has grown into one of Eastern Europe’s leading film events. While stating he does not feel betrayed, Zelensky expressed regret over declining US defense aid, noting that recent levels do not constitute genuine support.

Russian Strike Hits Lozova Warehouse, Killing 1, Injuring 2 — A Russian missile struck a commercial warehouse in Lozova, Kharkiv region, on Saturday, Oct. 24, killing a 45-year-old man and injuring two others aged 26 and 43, according to regional governor Oleh Syniehubov. Concurrently, a Russian strike on an infrastructure site in Zaporizhzhia injured two people and damaged vehicles.

In the Shadow of the Front — Reclaimed from Russian occupation in 2022, the villages beyond Kharkiv remain exposed to a war reaching farther behind the front line. Along the roads connecting these settlements, mobile anti-drone teams try to protect passing traffic and the few remaining residents.

Russian Border Strikes and EU EES Challenge Checkpoints — Speaking at a Prague security forum, State Border Guard Service of Ukraine (DPSU) official Andrii Ivanskyi reported that deliberate Russian strikes on western crossing points with Moldova, Romania, and Poland since late August, alongside hybrid threats like cyber interference and bomb hoaxes, are complicating border logistics. Concurrently, checkpoints are adapting to biometric delays from the EU’s new Entry/Exit System (EES).

US-Ukraine-Russia Talks Slated for Abu Dhabi or Switzerland — The next round of trilateral talks between delegations from the US, Ukraine, and the Russia could convene in Abu Dhabi or Switzerland within the next couple of weeks, a US official told Sky News. The consultations aim to prepare foundations for a prospective leader-level summit, though significant technical preparation remains.

US Senators Threaten Nomination Block Over Ukraine Starlink Curbs — Bipartisan US senators are preparing to halt confirmations of Donald Trump’s federal nominees until the White House ensures the restoration of full Starlink functionality for Ukraine’s military. The measure escalates an institutional confrontation over foreign policy toward Moscow ahead of the post-midterm lame-duck session, with lawmakers like Brian Fitzpatrick threatening agency funding cuts and officials’ dismissals.

Yatsenyuk condemned the White House’s commercial diesel pact with Moscow and the Graham Act waiver, arguing that Middle East instability drives oil inflation rather than Ukrainian refinery strikes.

Trump Signals Possible Follow-On Military Operation Against Iran — Speaking at a campaign rally in Florida on Friday, Oct. 23, US President Donald Trump stated that the US could execute another military operation against Iran, saying Washington “may do another little Epic Fury.” The statement comes amid sustained volatility across Middle Eastern maritime transit corridors and fuel markets ahead of the Nov. 3 US midterms.

Ukraine Confirms Hits on Proton Plant, Tolyatti and Yeysk Airfield — The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine officially confirmed precision strikes conducted on Oct. 23 and overnight into Oct. 24 targeting key military-industrial and aviation assets inside Russia. Hits were verified against the main production facility of JSC Proton-Elektroteks in Oryol, disrupting the manufacturing of components for Iskander-M ballistic missiles, S-71 cruise missiles, and Pantsir-S1 systems. Moldova Expels Russian Diplomat After Drone Crash — The Moldovan Ministry of Foreign Affairs declared a staff member of the Russian Embassy in Chișinău persona non grata on Friday, Oct. 23, following the crash of an explosive Russian Geran attack drone on Moldovan sovereign territory. President Maia Sandu condemned the aerial violation, noting the unmanned munition crashed in proximity to residential homes and an energy installation.

Ukraine Received Only 24 US Patriots in 90 Days — President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Ukraine received only 24 Patriot interceptors from the United States over the past three months, despite facing intense Russian ballistic attacks and requiring roughly 350 interceptor missiles per month. Noting that Russian forces launched over 20 ballistic missiles on Oct. 22 alone, Zelensky contrasted Kyiv’s acute munition shortfalls with the Middle East conflict, where partner nations expended roughly 2

Drones Hit Tolyatti Plant, Missiles Strike Oryol Defense Site — An overnight Ukrainian drone attack has struck the Tolyattikauchuk petrochemical plant in Russia’s Samara region, igniting a major blaze and forcing the evacuation of workers at the neighboring AvtoVAZ automotive factory. Concurrently, missiles struck the Proton defense microelectronics plant in Oryol, destroying a key workshop supplying components for T-90 and T-14 tanks, Pantsir-S1 systems, and Iskander-M and S-71 missiles.

Big Chill Between Turkey and Azerbaijan — Diplomatic relations between Turkey and Azerbaijan have deteriorated sharply following an address by Azerbaijan’s President Ilham Aliyev asserting sovereign independence, which Ankara has interpreted as a rebuke of Turkish influence. The dispute escalated with Baku imposing entry bans against 31 Turkish nationals, compounding earlier friction over Azerbaijan’s school headscarf ban. Turkish media expressed alarm over the total silence between Aliyev and T

Starlink, Starshield Speeds Exceed 161 km/h in Ukraine, MoD Says — Specialists from Ukraine’s Ministry of Defense and the Armed Forces confirmed on Saturday, Oct. 24, that Starlink and Starshield satellite terminals are now operating at velocities above 161 km/h (100 mph). Military communications teams continue tests at higher speeds to determine upper velocity limits and verify whether functionality has been unconditionally restored.

Rubio Says War Is About Donbas, Requires Diplomatic Compromise — US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated during a press conference on Thursday, Oct. 22, that the war in Ukraine is fundamentally about the Donbas – representing roughly 11 percent of the country that Russia cannot seize militarily and Ukraine legitimately refuses to cede for sovereignty and security reasons. Emphasizing that the conflict cannot be resolved militarily, Rubio asserted that an end to hostilities requires diplomatic c

Oleshky: The Kremlin’s Next Propaganda Spectacle? — A potential ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky could open the way for a Kremlin-controlled press tour and gaslighting operation designed to shift blame for the humanitarian crisis onto Ukraine. Past operations in Mariupol, Kherson, Bucha and elsewhere show a recurring method: create or exploit suffering, deny responsibility, select compliant witnesses, and present propaganda as independent reporting.

Trump Weighs 200% Tariffs on Ukraine and Russia, Doubts Impact — US President Donald Trump claimed that tariffs had previously ended five wars and suggested applying 200 percent duties to Ukraine and Russia, though he conceded the move would not work because the US does not import enough from either country.

Zelensky Ready to Freeze Front Line to Halt War, Rejects Land Cession — President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Ukraine is prepared to freeze combat operations along existing front lines to bring an immediate halt to the war, while firmly rejecting territorial concessions and vowing never to recognize occupied lands as Russian sovereign territory. Clarifying that Russian forces currently control 19.3 percent of Ukraine rather than 25 percent, Zelensky stressed that halting the war along the

2 Injured as Russian Strike Hits House in Kyiv — A Russian aerial attack damaged a private residential home in Kyiv’s northern Obolonskyi district early Saturday, Oct. 24, injuring two civilians, the Kyiv City Military Administration reported. An air raid alert was declared around 3:42 a.m. as turbojet drones entered capital airspace. Carney Warns Starlink Manipulation Puts Ukrainian Lives at Risk — Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney condemned reported Starshield speed restrictions affecting Ukraine’s military operations, warning of direct casualties and serious national security risks. He cited Russia’s deadly attacks on Kyiv and raised concerns about dependence on privately controlled satellite networks.

Zelensky Lays Out Ukraine’s Conditions for Lasting Peace — Zelensky outlines Ukraine’s conditions for lasting peace, calling for a powerful army backed by at least 10 years of international funding, firm US and European security guarantees, and a ceasefire before broader negotiations. He also warns of delayed Patriot deliveries and persistent Starlink restrictions while proposing trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi.

‘Interceptors Still Not Coming’ – Zelensky Says US Has Yet to Authorize Patriot Deliveries — President Zelensky warned that previously agreed Patriot interceptor deliveries remain delayed, leaving Ukraine short of critical air defenses against Russian ballistic attacks. He also warned that Starlink and Starshield speed restrictions continue to hamper Ukrainian military operations despite reports that services had been restored.

Monitoring channels reported disabled substations and widespread outages, while Russian-installed officials confirmed disruptions in Sevastopol.

Melania Trump Announces Oleshky Truce as Ukraine and Russia Agree to Civilian Evacuations — US First Lady Melania Trump has announced a localized ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky to enable humanitarian deliveries and civilian evacuations. The initiative builds on her earlier efforts to reunite Ukrainian children separated from their families during Russia’s war.

Russia Pounds Kramatorsk With Aerial Bombs – 1 Killed, 6 Injured, Including 3 Children — A Russian airstrike on a residential neighborhood in Kramatorsk killed one civilian and wounded six others, including three children. Three FAB-250 aerial bombs damaged at least 27 residential buildings.

Ukraine’s Battlefield Lessons Reshape How Bundeswehr Trains Its Combat Medics — According to an official report on Monday, Oct. 19, Germany’s armed forces are overhauling how they train their combat medics, evacuate casualties and protect field hospitals. Oleshky Evacuation: Russia Announces Kherson Frontline ‘Silence Regime’ — Russia’s top general, Valery Gerasimov, announced a “silence regime” along the Kherson front starting Oct. 27 for a humanitarian operation in occupied Oleshky, two days earlier than the date set by the White House. A separate report describes the exploitation of North Korean laborers, foreign women and Russian students working there.

1 Killed, 11 Injured as Russia Strikes Dnipropetrovsk Region Nearly 70 Times — Russian forces struck four districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region nearly 70 times on Friday, Oct. 23, killing one person and wounding 11. According to the head of the Dnipropetrovsk Regional Military Administration Oleksandr Hanzha, Dnipro faced the brunt of the attack, with a private house destroyed and a body recovered from the rubble.

Ukraine Ends Blanket Deferments, Ties Full Exemptions to Military Service — Ukraine’s government, led by Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi, has finalized an overhaul of its worker deferment system, effectively ending unconditional 100% deferments for defense and energy companies. The changes target firms created solely to shield workers from the draft, while companies could still defer all staff if they regularly send some of their employees to serve in the military.

White House Says Russia, Ukraine Agree to Oleshky Truce — The White House said Friday, Oct. 23, that Ukraine and Russia had agreed to a local ceasefire in occupied Oleshky in southern Ukraine’s Kherson region, beginning Oct. 29. The announcement credited US First Lady Melania Trump with mediating the agreement, which is intended to allow humanitarian aid into the city and prepare civilian evacuations. Kyiv and Moscow had not immediately commented.

Romania Blames Russia for Drone Strike That Sank Black Sea Ship — Romanian President Nicușor Dan blamed Russia for a drone strike that sank the Comoros-flagged Khoryv near Constanța on Oct. 23. The sinking follows a series of attacks on commercial shipping as NATO prepares to reinforce surveillance in the Black Sea.

All 4 Moscow Airports Halt Flights as Sheremetyevo Issues Air Raid Alert — Russia suspended arrivals and departures at Moscow’s four airports on Oct. 23. Sheremetyevo issued an air raid alert, while Vnukovo warned passengers of prolonged waits, including aboard aircraft.

‘We Are Christians, Good People’: Russian Media Tycoon Urges Nuclear Strike on Ukraine — Appearing on Piers Morgan’s show, Konstantin Malofeyev criticized Putin for not using nuclear weapons and proposed targeting Western arms depots in Ukraine. The media tycoon previously advocated a tactical nuclear attack followed by public executions.

Belarus Still Hosts Russian Drone Relays, Ukraine’s Border Service Says — Andriy Demchenko, spokesman for Ukraine’s State Border Guard Service (DPSU), said in a televised interview on Friday that Belarus continues to host relay stations used by Russian drones. He said border guards have not recorded Russian or Belarusian units moving toward the Ukrainian border. Ukraine said in June that the relays had stopped working, but Demchenko said in September that they were active again.

Abu Dhabi Considered for Ukraine-Russia-US Talks in November — Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Abu Dhabi is being considered for renewed talks between Ukraine, Russia and the United States. Moscow has proposed discussing postwar security, while Kyiv is seeking an early meeting and enforceable guarantees against another Russian attack.

443 Drones Downed: Russian Airfield, Chemical Plant and Tax Data Center Targeted in Overnight Attacks — Drone attacks reportedly damaged infrastructure near Voronezh’s Baltimor airfield, a chemical plant in Perm Krai and a Russian tax service data center in Nizhny Novgorod region. Russian officials reported three injuries and said 443 drones had been downed nationwide.

Ukraine Returns 270 in New POW Exchange — Ukraine has brought home 270 people in a prisoner exchange with Russia, including military personnel and nine civilians. Five of those released were previously believed to have died in the July 2022 attack on the Olenivka prison, Zelensky said.

Witkoff Meets Putin: the Upshot? — European and international media criticize Donald Trump’s Ukraine mediation efforts, warning that his envoy Steve Witkoff’s praise of Vladimir Putin undermines diplomatic credibility. Commentators argue that Moscow is exploiting US eagerness for a peace deal to buy time, weaken Ukraine and divide Western allies. They stress that Ukraine will resist surrender, while doubts grow over Trump’s motives, security guarantees and prospects for lasting peace.

Russian Diesel Tanker Heads to New York After Trump-Putin Deal — A shipment of around 40,000 metric tons of Russian diesel set sail for the US on Thursday, following a Trump-Putin agreement to resume Russian diesel exports. Its expected Nov. 7 arrival comes after the Nov. 3 elections, and the amount is estimated to last the US just shy of two hours of use.

Ukraine Still Recording Starshield Connectivity Losses at 161 Kph, Defense Ministry Source Says — Ukraine’s defense ministry says satellite connectivity losses at speeds of 161 kph are still in place, despite US President Donald Trump’s claim that SpaceX owner Elon Musk restored the service. US Reportedly Plans to ‘Offer’ Ukraine EU Membership for Dropping NATO Bid — A US peace proposal reportedly ‘offers’ Ukraine EU membership and investment in exchange for abandoning its NATO bid. The package also envisages economic incentives for Russia. No agreement has been announced, and EU accession would require approval from the bloc’s members.

One Dead, Three Missing From Ship in ‘Distress’ in Black Sea — Romania launched a rescue operation after a cargo ship carrying 13 Ukrainian and Azerbaijani crew members sent a distress signal in the Black Sea. Nine people were rescued and one body recovered, with three crew still missing, amid a series of suspected Russian drone attacks on shipping in the region.

US Reportedly Proposes Nord Stream Revival in Ukraine Peace Talks — US proposals reportedly include reviving Nord Stream, easing sanctions and expanding business ties with Russia. Ukrainian negotiators fear economic concessions could precede an end to the war, while access to Europe’s gas market remains outside Washington’s control.

Zelensky Yacht Fake: How Russia’s Doppelgänger Network Works — Russia’s Doppelgänger network tracked how fabricated stories about Ukraine reached Western audiences, according to an investigation by The Insider. Internal files included JD Vance’s remarks about a Ukrainian minister buying a yacht, alongside reports on other disinformation campaigns.

Russia to Unveil ‘Anti-Drone Dome’ at Africa Summit — Russia will pitch its planned “Anti-Drone Dome” air defense system to African partners at next week’s Moscow summit, even as Ukrainian drone strikes continue to hit Russian oil refineries and other critical infrastructure, exposing gaps in Moscow’s air defenses.

Austria Expels Four Russian Diplomats: Foreign Ministry — Austria has ordered four Russian diplomats to leave the country over activities deemed incompatible with their diplomatic status. The expulsions come amid heightened European concerns about Russian espionage following Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Denmark Delivers Over 50,000 Cannon Rounds for Ukraine’s F-16s — Ukraine’s Defense Ministry says Denmark delivered more than 50,000 rounds of 20 mm ammunition for its F-16 fighters. The ammunition is already being used in air-defense operations after Copenhagen redirected part of a planned sale with another country’s agreement.

Russia Pounds Kyiv’s Energy Infrastructure: How Are Residents Preparing for Winter? — As Russian attacks threaten Kyiv’s energy infrastructure ahead of winter, residents share their thoughts about power cuts, heating shortages and the city’s preparedness. While some are preparing to leave, most say they intend to stay but question whether the authorities are doing enough to protect the capital.

5 European Leaders Floated as Potential Negotiators With Putin — Five European leaders, including Italy’s Giorgia Meloni and Finland’s Alexander Stubb, are being considered to represent Europe in potential talks with Vladimir Putin as European capitals seek a greater role in efforts to end Russia’s war against Ukraine.

Oleksandr Levchenko: Financing Ukraine’s Recovery Must Combine Capital, Risk Management, and Responsible AI — Oleksandr Levchenko explains how risk-adjusted finance, digital resilience, and carefully governed AI can help attract investment and strengthen Ukraine’s postwar recovery. He also discusses the opportunities and limits of artificial intelligence in the financial sector.

Russia Strikes Odesa Energy Facility, Claims Naval Drone Sites Hit as Attacks Injure 2 Elsewhere — Russian attacks damaged energy and civilian infrastructure in southern Ukraine’s Odesa region overnight, while strikes on central Ukraine’s Poltava and Dnipropetrovsk regions damaged railway facilities, homes and other infrastructure. Two people were injured in the Dnipropetrovsk region, Ukrainian officials said.

A Prisoner Release From Hell: the Potentially Catastrophic Human Cost of Trump’s Deal — The release of Stephen Hubbard is now being used by Trump as a diplomatic trophy to justify the isolation and abandonment of Ukraine for an American realignment with Putin’s Russia.

Poland Probes Plot to Torch Drone Factory Supplying Ukraine — Polish prosecutors are investigating an alleged plot to set fire to Flytronic, a factory producing reconnaissance drones used by Ukraine, after a Russia-linked recruiter reportedly offered $30,000 for the attack. The case has been referred to Poland’s Internal Security Agency.

Drones Hit Occupied Luhansk, Disrupting Communications as Russia Strikes Ukrainian Power Plant — Drones struck communications infrastructure in Russian-occupied Luhansk early Oct. 23, disrupting services, while a Russian attack forced a DTEK thermal power plant to halt generation. Ukraine’s air defenses reported neutralizing 140 of 176 Russian drones launched since Thursday evening.

‘Not Another Budapest Memorandum’ – Kyiv Seeks US Security Guarantees Backed by Congress — President Volodymyr Zelensky says Ukraine is negotiating Article 5-style security guarantees with Washington that would require US congressional approval. Rejecting a repeat of the failed Budapest Memorandum, he calls for a comprehensive defense framework combining American commitments, NATO membership, European support and a strong Ukrainian military.

‘Putin Is Using Hitler’s Tactics’ – Ranking US Senator Slams Russian Attacks on Ukrainian Cities — Senator Jeanne Shaheen compares Russia’s bombardment of Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure to Hitler’s attacks on Britain, warning that Putin seeks to break civilian morale. She joins bipartisan criticism of US envoy Steve Witkoff for calling Putin a “humanitarian,” with Republican lawmakers responding, “WTF, Steve?”

Russia Launches Massive Drone Attack on Sumy as Moscow Continues Strikes Despite Peace Talks — Russian forces launched a massive drone attack on Sumy early Friday, Oct. 23, injuring at least two civilians and damaging residential areas. The assault followed deadly strikes on Kyiv and other Ukrainian regions as Moscow signaled readiness for renewed peace negotiations while continuing its bombardment.

‘Starshield Still Limited’ – Zelensky Says Restrictions Continue to Hamper Ukraine’s Drone Defenses — President Volodymyr Zelensky tells CNN that Ukraine’s Starshield military communications remain restricted despite reports of restored service, limiting its ability to intercept Russian drones. He confirms US missile-warning intelligence has resumed, urges more Patriot interceptors and opposes easing sanctions on Moscow.

Trump Says Musk Restored Ukraine’s Starshield — President Donald Trump says Elon Musk restored Ukraine’s military-grade Starshield satellite service after speed restrictions disrupted Ukrainian strike and interceptor drones. The US president declined to confirm reports that he personally intervened.

‘Putin Has Killed Thousands’ – Downing Street Rebukes Witkoff for Calling Russian Leader ‘Humanitarian’ — Downing Street rejects US envoy Steve Witkoff’s description of Vladimir Putin as a “humanitarian,” citing thousands killed in Russia’s war and systematic attacks on Ukraine’s civilian infrastructure.

‘More Money Means More Dead Ukrainians’ – Kasparov Warns Against Deals With Moscow — Garry Kasparov warns that exchanging Russian political prisoners for sanctions relief would allow Moscow to build more missiles and drones, while sharply criticizing the prospect of striking deals with Putin.
